script: For decades, people believed a stretch of ocean between Florida, Bermuda, and Puerto Rico was secretly swallowing ships and planes without a trace. The legend exploded in 1945, when Flight 19, five Navy bombers, vanished during a routine training mission, and the rescue plane sent to find them disappeared too. Newspapers called it cursed. Some blamed magnetic anomalies, others whispered about something stranger hiding beneath the waves. But investigators later found the real secret: the lead pilot got disoriented, his compass readings were misread, and a storm rolled in exactly when fuel was running out. Most other disappearances turned out to be ordinary storms, human error, and heavy shipping traffic, wildly exaggerated by writers chasing a good story. The ocean was never cursed. The real secret was how easily a good story can outlive the truth.
